title: Tone.js — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Tone.js's rich face: the second Gotcha's claim put under plain Web Audio — sixty frequency pushes a second against the same equation run per sample, measured in what is rendered and handed to the ear blind — and the Recipe's shipped explorer gathered beside its own lines. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.
grain: The page's own ## grain. Only Gotchas and Recipes carry pieces; Gotchas is one section holding both dated gotchas and the community list, so its one stamp covers all of it.

offers.what: The second Gotcha's reason ("because the parameter automation is rendered at audio rate by Web Audio's internal scheduling") isn't what makes it work. setValueAtTime holds each value until the next push, so the frequency is a staircase at the frame rate: rendered sample by sample, but still a staircase. It works because the oscillator turns the staircase into a phase with no jumps, and the beat it has to follow is a few hertz, slow next to 60. Measured in Chromium's Web Audio (plain OscillatorNode, not Tone), Δf = 2 Hz: beat 1.733 · 0.873 · 0.282 Hz pushed against 1.732 · 0.872 · 0.282 per sample (Adler predicts 1.732 · 0.872 · 0.282) at K = 0.5 · 0.9 · 0.99; both lock at K = 1.00 = K_c on a 0.01 grid; the staircase's traces 60 Hz from the tones sit at −72.5 dB re the tones (per sample −140.1). Suggested reason: the oscillator smooths the 60 Hz staircase into its phase, and the beat it follows is far slower than the frame rate.

"Sample-coherent enough for audio-rate carriers in the 100–500 Hz range" names the wrong variable. The carrier doesn't matter; the frame rate against the coupling and the gap does. Two edges, measured: (a) the lock shudders once K·cos φ* passes rate/2π, onset K = 9.6 · 4.9 · 3.4 Hz at 60 · 30 · 20 pushes a second (predicted 9.60 · 4.88 · 3.34 from the Euler step), so the explorer's 0–6 Hz slider is safe at 60 frames and not at 30, nor at its own 1/20 s clamp (at K = 6 the locked gap swings 19.5 Hz at 30, 24.2 at 20, 0.00 at 60); (b) with the tones more than half the frame rate apart the push aliases the beat: at 120 and 220 Hz with K = 6, both inside the explorer's sliders, the pushed tone carries a line 20 Hz off at −19.2 dB where the coupled one has −124.4. Also the staircase rises with the coupling: −35.8 dB at Δf 12.5, K 6 (per sample −51.9). Suggest: enough while the beat stays well under half the frame rate and K stays under about rate/2π (9.6 Hz at 60 frames a second).

The pushed tones aren't coupled to each other: the model is, and the tones follow it open loop. The beat still stops, but the locked phase gap is the model's plus whatever the model missed, and nothing pulls it back. Measured with K rising 0 → 1.5 over 6 s: on schedule, the locked chord is 0.4 dB under the coupled pair's (the explorer steps its phases before it pushes, so the tones run a frame behind its model: 2π·Δf/60 = 0.209 rad off φ*); with ±1 ms frame jitter and pushes on 128-sample render quanta, 0.4–0.5 dB under; with one stalled frame of 60–500 ms during the drift (dt clamps at 0.05 s), 0.1 to 16.1 dB under. Worth one line in the Gotcha: what it calls sample-coherent holds the lock's frequency, not its phase.

K_c = |Δf|/2 is right with K in hertz, as the explorer runs it: dθ/dt = 2π(f + K·sin Δθ). With the equation as the Gotcha writes it, dθ/dt = ω + K·sin(Δθ), K is in rad/s and the threshold is |Δω|/2 = π·|Δf|. Name K's unit (Hz), or write the equation with the 2π outside.

"Raising K past K_c first slows the beating, then collapses it": the slowing comes before K_c, on the way up, as √(Δf² − (2K)²) (measured 1.733 · 0.873 · 0.282 Hz at K = 0.5 · 0.9 · 0.99 with Δf = 2); past K_c it stops. Suggest: as K rises toward K_c the beating slows, and past it the beating stops.

The shipped explorer (Kuramoto Coupling/two-oscillators-coupling-explorer-audio.html, the Recipe's output) says in its own note that each frequency is f_j + (K/2π)·sin(θ_other − θ_j), but its code adds K·sin (K in Hz, as its slider is labelled), and the code is what the measurements match. Its readout "instantaneous beating rate" shows |f_A,inst − f_B,inst|, which below K_c swings between Δf − 2K and Δf + 2K rather than the beat heard, √(Δf² − 4K²). The note wants the /2π dropped; the readout wants a name like "frequency gap now". The fix is in the explorer file, not in this page's text.

pieces.title: sixty pushes a second, against the equation per sample
pieces.near: is enough to feel Kuramoto locking on two audio-rate sines
pieces.caption: **The second Gotcha, tested under Tone.** Five steps: two sines beating; coupled the page's way (sixty setValueAtTime pushes a second); the same pair run per sample in a worklet, with the pushed staircase drawn; then the test, rendered offline and measured. In the Gotcha's own situation the claim holds: same beat rates to a thousandth of a hertz, the same lock K, a staircase 73 dB down. Its reason and its condition don't hold as written: the lock shudders above K ≈ rate/2π, a gap over half the frame rate aliases, and a stalled frame shifts the locked chord's loudness for good. The last step is a blind listen with a control round, because "enough to feel" is a claim about a listener. Chromium's numbers, not Tone's.

pieces.title: two-oscillator audio coupling explorer · Tone.js
pieces.caption: **The Recipe's own output.** The Study-tier explorer the Recipe describes, as it shipped into Kuramoto Coupling's bundle: two Tone.Oscillator sines, a K slider, a scope and the drift / pulling in / lock readout. It loads Tone 15.0.4 from the shelf's CDN, so it plays where the CDN is reachable. Its note's (K/2π) and its "instantaneous beating rate" readout are carried as an offer; the Gotchas piece above rebuilds the same pair without Tone.
